# ezghcloud_dns_zone (Resource)

A public DNS zone. Destroying it deletes its record sets; remove record sets that other EZGH services manage (such as a domain authorization's validation records) first.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "ezghcloud_dns_zone" "main" {
  project_id = var.project_id
  domain     = "example.com"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `domain` (String) Domain name of the zone in lowercase, such as example.com, without a trailing dot. Changing it replaces the zone.
- `project_id` (String) Project identifier. Changing it replaces the zone.

### Optional

- `dnssec_enabled` (Boolean) Sign the zone with DNSSEC. Defaults to false.
- `tags` (Map of String) Zone tags. The API can't change a zone's tags, and replacing a zone would delete its record sets, so a change is refused at plan.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Zone ID (zon_).
- `nameservers` (List of String) Nameservers to delegate the domain to.
- `status` (String) pending until the zone's ownership is verified, then active.
- `verification` (Attributes) The TXT record that proves control of the domain while the zone is pending. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--verification))

<a id="nestedatt--verification"></a>
### Nested Schema for `verification`

Read-Only:

- `txt_name` (String) TXT record name.
- `txt_value` (String) TXT record value.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import ezghcloud_dns_zone.main prj_xxxxxxxxxxxx/zon_xxxxxxxxxxxx
```
